title: Consumer Care Note — The Portfolio Affordability Test for Payment Arrangements
content:
Payment Arrangements of a type that requires a budget review are tested against the consumer's whole portfolio of arrangements, not against the new plan alone.

## The rule

For plan types whose budget review is required, the consumer's stated net monthly household income is taken and stored on the plan, and the test is applied across the consumer's whole portfolio of arrangements rather than to the new plan alone. The stated income is the consumer's own statement, taken before the plan is set up, and it belongs to the consumer who owes the plan.

Each plan's monthly-equivalent installment is its installment amount multiplied by the periods per year of its payment frequency — 52 for weekly, 26 for biweekly, 12 for monthly — and divided by 12, rounded to the cent.

The portfolio total is the sum of the monthly-equivalent installments of all of the consumer's plans in pending authorization, active or suspended status, on every placed account.

A new plan, or a restructured plan, is allowed only when the portfolio total, with the plan's own monthly-equivalent installment replacing any earlier amount for the same plan, is no more than the type's income share ceiling percent of the stated net monthly income (that ceiling amount rounded to the cent).

When the test fails, the installment cannot be raised to fit and a longer plan type or a smaller installment within the type's minimums must be chosen; when no type passes, the consumer is offered a promise-to-pay or the hardship programme rather than an unaffordable plan.

Plan types whose income share ceiling is 0.0 apply no affordability test, and their installments still count toward the portfolio total of any later tested plan. Whether a type requires the budget review, and its ceiling, are the type's product figures.

## Condition — judgement — result

| Condition | Judgement | Result |
|---|---|---|
| The type's ceiling is 0.0 | No test applies | The plan is not held to the test |
| Portfolio total with the plan is no more than the ceiling amount | Test passes | The plan or restructure is allowed by this rule |
| Portfolio total with the plan is above the ceiling amount | Test fails | The installment is not raised to fit; a longer type or a smaller installment within the minimums is chosen |
| No type passes | — | A promise-to-pay or the hardship programme is offered |

## Worked figure (hypothetical inputs)

A consumer states a net monthly household income of 3000.00 and asks for an Extended Installment Plan, whose ceiling in this illustration is 20.0 percent: the ceiling amount is 600.00. The consumer already has an active plan paid biweekly at 120.00 on another account: 120.00 multiplied by 26 and divided by 12 is 260.00. A proposed monthly installment of 300.00 has a monthly equivalent of 300.00; 260.00 plus 300.00 is 560.00, no more than 600.00, so the test passes. A proposed 350.00 would bring the total to 610.00, above 600.00, and the test fails.

A broken plan does not enter the portfolio total; a pending plan does.
